raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Rue de Rivoli behind, head for Place des Vosges, about an eleven-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Think back over the walk you've just made.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"You began at the Bastille, a medieval castle that took thirteen years to build, was finished in 1382, and then came down in just four months in 1789 — its fall freeing seven prisoners on the fourteenth of July.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"From there you crossed the Marais, whose name simply means swamp, into the district that Henri IV's reign turned into the hometown of the French aristocracy.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Almost opposite the Church of Saint-Louis–Saint-Paul, this small neighborhood square faces rue d'Ormesson at the end of rue Caron.","source_id":"505d7f06-cd49-4b35-9803-7cb447744e6d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Find a bench in the garden near the children's play area, watch them play à la française, and listen to the Hebrew, Yiddish, and Arabic drifting past — because this modest neighborhood square was, for nearly two centuries, the single most fashionable one in Paris.","source_id":"e8583eae-9019-4ca0-a94c-e2a4f3ff26ae","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"If it's cold, duck into Café Ma Bourgogne on the northwest corner; the view through the window is nearly as good.","source_id":"e8583eae-9019-4ca0-a94c-e2a4f3ff26ae","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The central pavilion on the south side, at no. 1, is called the Pavillon du Roi, the King's Pavilion — and yet no king ever lived in it.","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It was too small for the king and his retinue, so the very first resident was his concierge, the gatekeeper.","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Since 1666 it's been rented out to a run of tenants, and today it's carved into apartments reached by ugly stairs and an elevator crammed into the right-hand side of the central arcade — an eighteenth-century intrusion that still rankles, because it blocks part of the view down the rue de Birague.","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The writer Germain Brice was complaining about it as early as 1752, arguing the pavilion's three arcades should be torn down so the Louis XIII statue could be seen all the way from the rue Saint-Antoine: 'It has to hurt,' he wrote, 'to see one of the three arcades blocked to make a nasty stairway… we have such little care for public embellishments in Paris.'","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Look up anyway — the balcony here is stone rather than wrought iron, and a bust of Henri IV watches the square from above.","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Walk through the arcade to the rue de Birague side and you'll find the king's arms and initials above the arches, still there from the original construction.","source_id":"fd3ba503-bd42-42b9-abde-6e14675e08db","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"At no. 3, press the button marked porte and step into the courtyard behind — the first in the square to be restored, and the only one with brick walls inside.","source_id":"e8f49a18-cf3f-482c-809a-c14be85433cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Except the brick isn't brick.","source_id":"e8f49a18-cf3f-482c-809a-c14be85433cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Look closely and it's painted, trompe l'oeil, right down to the pipes in the corners — pink where they cross the red 'brick,' ivory where they run against the stone trim.","source_id":"e8f49a18-cf3f-482c-809a-c14be85433cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The building rose in 1613 on the old stables of the Hôtel des Tournelles, two huge bronze urns still stand against the back wall, and the ground-floor shop now belongs to Issey Miyake.","source_id":"e8f49a18-cf3f-482c-809a-c14be85433cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Just off the northeast corner, at 36 rue des Tournelles, the richest and most glamorous people in Paris kept coming back to one salon — and it belonged to Ninon de l'Enclos.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Born in 1620, she had, like every Frenchwoman of the seventeenth century, exactly four paths open to her: wife, nun, prostitute, or governess.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The convent lasted about a year before that vocation fell to the ground, and she went home to host what became a fabled literary salon.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"She refused to marry and lived as a celebrated courtesan, entertaining a stream of lovers — famous nobles right alongside the very priests and bishops who denounced her from the Sunday pulpit, offended less by the courtesan than by the woman and author who openly scorned organized religion.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Molière said she had 'the keenest sense of the absurd of anyone I know,' and his Les Précieuses Ridicules skewered exactly the idle chatter of the salons and their fawning salonnards.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It was her influence, more than her transgressive sexual mores, that frightened the pious Queen Anne of Austria, mother of Louis XIV, who had Ninon locked up in a convent for a few months.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"'Feminine virtue,' Ninon observed, 'is nothing but a convenient masculine invention.'","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Her guests hung on lines like that — the memoirist Saint-Simon among them, quietly taking notes.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And when she died, she left money to a nine-year-old boy she'd once met, so he could buy books; his name was Voltaire.","source_id":"d05022a7-6cc7-4f05-bef6-ff252f250243","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And that closes the loop, back where we started.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Thank you for coming along with me today; when you're ready, take your time and keep exploring on your own.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4}]}
